posts.title: Getting Packages Into a Closed Network: pip and npm, Offline
posts.summary: On an air-gapped network, installing packages usually breaks at the handover, not at the install. Three causes — transitive dependencies, OS/CPU/version tags, and install scripts that reach back out — plus pip's wheelhouse and npm's three carry-in methods, with real commands, real failure messages, measured sizes and a pre-handover checklist.

posts.title: Getting a Grip on the Wheel: Keeping Vibe Coding From Coming Apart
posts.summary: Vibe coding is harder to sustain than to start. Context rot, silently broken features and secret leaks don't happen because the model is weak; they happen because verification, rules and permissions aren't layered underneath. Six setup steps — from a Git safety net to model and cost routing — plus a routine for each way things go wrong.
